dateline: Bamako / Kidal / Goubré / Tadjmart / Djibo / Diapaga — 2012–Present
heroHeadline: Day 26: Africa Corps Accused of Banned Cluster Bomb Use in Kidal Region; JNIM Claims Goubré IDP Camp Massacre (72 Civilians); Bamako Siege Holds
heroSubtitle: Two major developments define May 23–24, 2026: (1) CLUSTER BOMB ACCUSATION: On May 23, multiple outlets reported that Africa Corps/FAMa aircraft dropped Russian-made RBK-500 cluster bombs on Tadjmart hamlet near Aguelhoc (Kidal Region) during the night of May 16–17 — confirmed by RFI weapons specialist analysis of ShOAB-0.5 submunitions. One child was killed and three women were injured; a second strike hit near Oubder (Timbuktu Region). The Malian government dismissed coverage as 'media terrorism'; Africa Corps and Mali are not CCM signatories. The FLA is collecting unexploded remnants as evidence. The cluster bomb revelation adds a critical IHL dimension to the sustained aerial campaign on FLA/JNIM-held Kidal (10+ strikes in recent days). (2) GOUBRÉ IDP CAMP MASSACRE: On May 24, JNIM claimed responsibility for its May 22 attack on the Goubré displaced persons camp, Centre-Nord Region, Burkina Faso — one of the most severe single atrocities against internally displaced people in the conflict's 14-year history. HRW documented 80 killed: 72 civilians (45 men, 23 women, 2 girls, 2 boys) and 8 VDP fighters, plus ~40 injured. The camp housed ~3,500 displaced persons who had already fled earlier JNIM violence; it was shut down following the massacre. UN Humanitarian Coordinator for Burkina Faso condemned the attack and confirmed an aid worker was killed. BAMAKO SIEGE (Day 26): At least 3 of 6 supply corridors remain disrupted per Amnesty International; IRC emergency response active; WFP suspended; Manantali power grid degraded. The US Embassy in Bamako's enhanced security alert (issued May 19) remains active through May 31, warning of route closures, fortified positions, and heightened threats near the airport. The AES Unified Force (15,000 authorized strength) has not arrested the multi-country simultaneous strike tempo that has defined the crisis since April 25: Bamako siege (Day 26), Kidal aerial campaign, Ménaka urban standoff (Day 26), Djibo (May 11), Diapaga (May 13), Goubré (May 22), and JNIM's confirmed Benin front (Porga, May 7). No ceasefire negotiations reported as of May 24, 2026.
